components.title: Filter orders by date range
components.what: Select all orders with order_date from 2026-05-09 to 2026-06-14 inclusive, regardless of status, then remove exact duplicate rows (same order_id and all fields) so each order counts once.

components.title: Compute median unit_price
components.what: Calculate the median of unit_price over the deduplicated, date-filtered set of orders.

asked: The stated dedup rule is given in the revenue preamble; does it govern this median question too, and if the three identical O2606 rows were instead each counted (N=25), what would the median become? State which convention you are applying and why.

Confirm whether any two in-range orders share the same unit_price (i.e., whether the sorted list has ties that could affect which row is identified as the 12th), and name the orders at sorted positions 11, 12, and 13.
replies:
1. The dedup rule is stated as a general property of the orders table ("a few exact duplicate rows... count once"), not scoped only to revenue, so it applies here too: N=23 is correct. If counted as N=25 (not following the rule), sorted list would have two extra 49.48 entries, median would be average of 13th/14th values = (49.48+55.99)/2... recomputing: inserting two more 49.48 into list shifts middle; with N=25 median is the 13th value. List becomes 5.02,5.86,7.34,15.96,19.62,23.10,35.18,36.33,37.21,49.48,49.48,49.48,51.50,55.99,60.26,... 13th value=51.50. So alternate convention gives 51.50, but the correct one per stated rule is still 55.99 with N=23.
2. No ties exist among the 23 in-range unit_prices (all distinct). Positions 11,12,13 in sorted order are O2887(51.50), O2561(55.99), O2500(60.26).
